correct_completion: she would have caught the train.
full_sentence: Had she left earlier, she would have caught the train.
acceptable_variants: she would have arrived on time.
she would not have missed the meeting.

options.text: she would have missed the train.
options.why_wrong: Missing the train contradicts the logic of leaving earlier. The result must be the opposite of the unreal past condition.

options.text: she would catch the train yesterday.
options.why_wrong: 'Would' with a past time expression does not match the inverted third conditional structure, which needs 'would have' plus a past participle.

options.text: she would have caught the train.
she catches the train every day.
options.why_wrong: This is a habitual present statement. It does not complete the hypothetical past condition started by 'had she left'.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional with 'had' before the subject
explanation: In an inverted third conditional, 'had' moves before the subject and replaces 'if'. The main clause then needs 'would have' plus a past participle to express an unreal past result. Speakers may be tempted to use a simple tense here, but the structure requires the perfect form.
